result.summary: The image shows a typical urban residential intersection with sidewalks but lacking marked pedestrian crossings. While stop signs provide some traffic control, the presence of parked vehicles near the corners creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted crosswalks, which fails to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and crossing locations.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and along the left curb line

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly delineate pedestrian paths.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: This residential street features a narrow sidewalk and a low-speed environment, but lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure like marked crossings or curb ramps. The presence of large parked vehicles creates significant visual obstructions for anyone attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles, specifically the black pickup truck in the foreground, significantly block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks and curb ramps forces pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations without designated safety features.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Installation of high-visibility crosswalk markings and ADA-compliant curb ramps to provide safe and accessible crossing points.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Adding street trees to provide shade and create a vertical element that helps to naturally calm traffic speeds.

result.summary: A residential street with sidewalks and mature trees, but lacking marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices. Parked cars along the curb create significant visual obstructions between the sidewalk and the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars and mature trees along the curb line block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross mid-block without protection.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at corners to shorten crossing distances and prevent parking too close to intersections.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection with narrow streets and continuous sidewalks. While the low-speed nature of the street is beneficial, safety is reduced by faded crosswalk markings and significant visual obstructions from a large tree and building corners.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted lines for the crosswalk are significantly worn and faint, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the side street in the center-right foreground.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree and the corner of the brick building block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and vehicles approaching the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and mid-ground at the corner.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the faded markings to continental or ladder-style pavement markings to increase the visibility of the pedestrian crossing.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions and manage vegetation near the corner to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Tactile Warning Surfaces
interventions.description: Install truncated domes on the existing curb ramps to assist pedestrians with visual impairments in identifying the street edge.
